data_status: STRICT MODE: this dataset contains only values that were compared with, or ingested directly from, retrieved sources: JPL (SSD, SBDB, NHATS), NASA (NSSDC fact sheets and mission catalog, Small Spacecraft SoA report 2026, SLS page, Apollo 11 press kit, NTRS papers, data.nasa.gov), ULA, ESA, NIST, and the Launch Library 2 aggregator. Records carry source_authority/confidence where the source is an aggregator or vendor-reported compilation. Recalled, estimated and fictional values (optimizer catalog, costs, engine/vehicle specs without a retrievable source, the user-supplied SpaceX table) are not included. Derived values are computed only from verified inputs and are labelled derived.

record.name: Mars Descent Imager (MARDI)
record.description: The MARs Descent Imager (MARDI) is designed to take pictures of the martian surface below the rover as it descends for landing. The primary objectives of MARDI are to determine the exact location of the landing and provide a geologic and engineering-geologic framework of the landing site for early operations. MARDI MARDI is mounted to the fore-port side of the MSL rover, even with the bottom of the rover chassis. It points towards the ground in the rover coordinate frame and therefore downward during the descent phase. Imaging starts after heat shield separation and continues until touchdown. The camera takes approximately 5 frames/second, written into a flash memory for later transmission to Earth. The field of view is 70 x 55 degrees (1600 x 1200 pixels), ranging from 2.4 x 1.8 km (1.5 m/pixel) at 2 km altitude, to 2.4 x 1.8 m (1.5 mm/pixel) at 2 m altitude. Instantaneous field of view (IFOV) is approximately 0.76 milliradians. For more detailed information, see: http://msl-scicorner.jpl.nasa.gov/Instruments/MARDI/
